extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in crisis informatics, misinformation, public health communication, and computational social science
extracted.subtask_short: analyzing health rumors on social media
extracted.subtask_description: Quantitative and qualitative analysis of health-related rumors and debunking activities on Weibo during the COVID-19 crisis, comparing 'dread' and 'wish' rumor types, debunker roles, rhetorical and functional strategies, and debunking effectiveness over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health rumor typology (wish vs dread)
rubrics_metrics.description: Health rumors are categorized into dread and wish types according to people’s underlying concerns (DiFonzo et al. 2012). Dread rumors invoke fearsome consequences (e.g., microwave use can spread cancer), while wish rumors promote favorable outcomes (e.g., vitamin can cure cancer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these two types separately in analysis because they differ in content, psychological impact, dissemination patterns, and how debunking affects them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection timeframe and corpus source
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a temporally-bounded social media corpus; this study used Weibo posts from Jan 1, 2020 to May 1, 2020 provided by Qingbo Big Data (100,159,355 unique posts from 26,927,690 users).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the exact time window and source; include fields like textual content, timestamp, retweet flag, media attachments, post and author IDs to enable deduplication and tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying rumor topics from fact-checking archives
rubrics_metrics.description: Compile a comprehensive list of pandemic-related rumors from archives of popular fact-checking websites (this study scraped 5,958 fact-checking articles from eleven Chinese websites). Manually inspect topic and veracity and remove items confirmed as not being rumors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage authoritative fact-checking sources to seed rumor topics; manual inspection is required to filter false positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation protocol and inter-annotator agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Two annotators (native speakers) identified health rumors and labeled their types independently with Cohen’s kappa reported (κ = 0.86 for identifying health rumors; κ = 0.81 for labeling wish/dread). Conflicts were resolved via negotiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report inter-annotator agreement; use independent annotation plus a conflict-resolution step to ensure label reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrieval via logical expressions with iterative screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Use logical expressions (e.g., Banana AND Prevent AND (Corona OR Virus)) to retrieve rumor-related posts. Annotators craft initial expressions, retrieve 100 random samples to verify, and iteratively refine expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iteratively refine queries with human inspection; do not rely solely on recall—prioritize high precision through manual screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision-based screening threshold (10% sampling, precision > 0.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: After retrieval, screen results by sampling 10% of retrieved posts; if precision fails to reach 0.9, repeat the screening and refinement process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 10% sampling and require precision ≥ 0.9 as a stopping criterion to ensure high-quality retrieval. Do not use recall as the primary quality control in this pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and detection of 'debunk' vs 'discuss' posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide posts into two exclusive classes: debunk (counter-rumor microblog messages) and discuss (the rest). Debunking posts tend to explicitly declare denials (e.g., 'this is not true') or flag misinformation (e.g., 'this is a rumor').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive regular expressions of debunking indicators from annotator inspection, automatically mark posts with such indicators, and iteratively improve with the 10%/precision>0.9 screening procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: User role categorization (individual, organization, government, media)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize user accounts into four types based on platform verification codes and account metadata: individuals (including verified individuals), organizations (enterprises, institutions, apps, schools, websites), government agencies, and media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merge platform-provided categories into the four roles for comparative analysis; provide examples and mapping (e.g., 'Police departments' -> Government, 'Xinhua News' -> Media).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent variables for dissemination patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure rumor dissemination via: number of posts (volume), number of unique users, duration (minutes between earliest and last post in a post set), and proportion of negative posts (negativity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply log transformation to highly skewed DVs (volume, users, duration) before regression analyses; use an external sentiment API to compute negativity proportion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal propagation speed curves
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize dynamic spread by plotting the minutes required for a rumor to reach various exposure levels (e.g., number of posts) and compare wish vs dread and discuss vs debunk subsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fine-grained time bins (e.g., minutes) to reveal short-term dynamics and identify extreme rumors (those exceeding thresholds like 10K posts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-variable linear regression and hypothesis testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use single-variable linear regression models with rumor type or debunker type as independent variables and DVs like volume/timeliness as dependent variables; complement with t-tests and Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) tests to assess mean and distribution differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report β coefficients, significance levels, and R-squared; interpret both distributional and mean differences using KS-test and t-test respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional preference metrics for debunking posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture posting behaviors via binary/continuous indicators: retweet (use of retweet feature), duplicate (textual duplication vs earlier posts), image (includes image), video (includes video), and length (text length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect duplicates using SimHash; analyze metadata across all debunking posts (this study used N=238,554 observations) and model with appropriate regressions (logistic for binary, linear for continuous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical preference coding (Logos, Pathos, Sarcasm, Source)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code rhetorical strategies adapted from Aristotelian persuasion: stating facts (Logos), expressing strong emotions (Pathos), sarcasm, and citing credible sources. Construct codebook via inductive/deductive coding (200 samples) and formally code a larger sample (1,025 posts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow multiple strategy codes per post; report coding percentages and inter-coder reliability (Cohen’s kappa for strategies reported: 0.509, 0.699, 0.692, 0.738 respectively). Use logistic regression for these binary DVs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement metrics for debunkers (volume and timeliness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure debunker engagement by number of debunking posts authored (volume) and average timeliness (time in minutes between a debunking post and the first post in that post set).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert timeliness to days for interpretation; compare means across user roles and rumor types and test significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) with coherence-guided topic number selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply LDA separately for wish and dread post sets and select the number of topics based on coherence measures (e.g., coherence improved little beyond 8 topics for dread with score 0.528; best for wish was 20 with score 0.510).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate verb and noun analyses; remove domain-high-frequency words before visualization (e.g., 'virus', 'corona'). Select top words per topic for word clouds and qualitative interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-series pre-processing and exclusion criteria for causality testing
rubrics_metrics.description: When testing Granger causality between debunking and discussion trends per rumor topic: (1) aggregate counts in six-hour bins; (2) remove topics with a gap >1 week between consecutive steps; (3) ensure stationarity (ADF test p < 0.05) and absence of problematic autocorrelation (Durbin-Watson).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude topics failing stationarity or showing problematic autocorrelation before fitting VAR models for Granger causality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granger causality testing with VAR lag selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct vector autoregressive (VAR) models using n lags of both series; select lag n that maximizes VAR model likelihood and use Granger causality test (p-value threshold e.g., p < 0.05) to evaluate whether debunking trends predict discussion trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform tests per-topic and report the proportion of topics with significant Granger-causal relationships to generalize across rumor pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppression ratio as measure of debunking effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a suppression ratio metric to quantify how declines of rumor discussion posts vary with different factors (e.g., rumor types and debunker roles) and over time, thereby assessing the temporal suppression effect of debunking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use suppression ratio alongside causality results to capture time-sensitive effectiveness; adapt the measure to different temporal scales (e.g., 1m, 20m, 3h, 12h, 1D, 7D, 30D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality control and screening procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality control steps include iterative refinement of retrieval/regex, sampling 100 for initial retrieval checks, 10% screening with precision threshold >0.9, and having a third annotator sample when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and report sampling sizes and thresholds; repeat screening cycles until precision criterion is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical treatment of skewed variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Because volume, user counts, and duration are highly skewed, apply log transformation prior to regression analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transform skewed DVs to better satisfy regression assumptions and interpret coefficients accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling choices for binary vs continuous dependent variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Use logistic regression for binary DVs (e.g., rhetorical strategy presence) and linear regression for continuous DVs (e.g., text length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate statistical model for the outcome variable type and report coefficients, significance, and (pseudo) R-squared as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and interpreting coder reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Report Cohen’s kappa for annotation tasks and for each coded rhetorical strategy (examples in paper: 0.509, 0.699, 0.692, 0.738).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use kappa values to qualify the reliability of categorical annotations and be transparent about lower kappas (e.g., 0.509) in interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling limitations and causal inference caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that analyses are retrospective and correlational and therefore cannot determine causation; low R-squared in some regressions may reflect contextual complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement observational analyses with controlled experiments or interviews where possible; interpret suppression/correlation results cautiously and report potential confounders (e.g., new events diverting attention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical risk-communication guidelines derived from analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations include: understand public health concerns to address information needs timely; maintain debunking efforts for both dread and wish misinformation; avoid risky debunking practices like 'post first, check later'; consider platform interventions to break rumor echo chambers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate empirical findings into operational guidelines for authorities and platforms, balancing timeliness, accuracy, and audience trust.
